title: Batch-splitting load spike — on-call handoff and weekly update
content:
Date: 2029-07-18 to 2029-07-21
Author: Priya Shah (serving-runtime) — on-call rotation handoff + weekly update
Attendees: Priya Shah, Marcus Li, Dana Ortiz, Evan Brooks, Lina Vakil (notes)

TL;DR
- We saw repeated short-lived load spikes (10–30s) during the last three on-call shifts that correlate with an uptick in batch-splitting events. Those spikes increase p95 latency by ~220ms and cause a 2.8% CPU busy bump on kernel hosts.
- Root cause hypothesis: interaction between the dynamic batch-splitting heuristic and the new KV-cache compression fallback for long sequences. In some sequences, estimated token footprint is underpredicted, triggering a split late in queueing, which forces extra kernel re-schedules and KV deserialization overhead.
- Mitigations in place: temporary throttling of batch-splitting (backoff to 12s window), disable KV-cache compression fallback for sequences >1024 tokens in the canary pool.

Timeline / symptoms observed
- 2029-07-18 03:14 UTC: first repeating spike, observed across 3 kernel hosts in west-2; spike lasted ~18s.
- 2029-07-18 04:00–08:00 UTC: repeated small spikes at ~30–45min intervals.
- 2029-07-19: more pronounced during mixed short+long sequence traffic (midnight PDT).
- 2029-07-20 09:10 UTC: introduced temporary mitigations listed below. Post-mitigation telemetry shows reduction in p95 latency delta and eliminated the longest tail events.

Telemetry snapshot (pre-mitigation average vs spike windows)
- normal p50/p95 generation latency: 42ms / 128ms
- during spike p50/p95: 48ms / 348ms (p95 increased by ~220ms)
- kernel host CPU busy: baseline 64% -> spike 66.8% (+2.8%)
- error rate (462 client errors traceable to resource contention): baseline 0.12% -> spike 0.9%
- batch-split events per minute (ws1-west-2 canary pool): baseline 2.1 bpm -> spike 28.4 bpm

What changed recently (relevant deploys)
- 2029-07-10: kernel scheduler tweak to prefer latency: rollout 80% — should reduce preemption but changed when splits occur.
- 2029-07-12: KV-cache histogram compression fallback merged (PR #1689) — compresses large cached segments and falls back to heavier deserialize path for >8KB segments.
- 2029-07-15: inference policy change for mixed-sequence prioritization (experimental on canary).

Root-cause hypotheses (ranked)
1) Underestimated memory/slot footprint for sequences with many sparse KV pages after compression fallback. The batch-split heuristic uses an amortized token-size estimator; compression reduces on-disk size but increases peak memory and CPU on decompress path. Late splits then trigger extra kernel handoffs.
2) Race between KV prefetch coalescer and splitting decision window leading to double-deserialize: prefetch writes claim cache entry while split cancels/reshuffles request ownership, causing both sides to deserialize the same large KV chunk.
3) Kernel scheduling change moved split decision slightly later in the pipeline; combined with (1) this exposes the CPU/latency amplification.

Experiments and quick tests run (notes)
- 2029-07-19 11:00 UTC: Canary A — disable compression fallback for sequences >1024 tokens. Result: batch-split spike count fell by 63% in canary group over 6 hours.
- 2029-07-19 15:30 UTC: Canary B — force earlier split decision (checkpoint at queue-time rather than pre-schedule). Result: p95 improved by 110ms but throughput fell 3.2% for heavy sequence traffic.
- 2029-07-20 01:40 UTC: Add metric dimension batch_split_reason (values: policy_threshold, mem_estimate, kernel_backpressure). Observation: 72% of split events during spikes classified as mem_estimate.

Temporary mitigations (deployed 2029-07-20)
- Apply conservative backoff to batch-splitting: min-window increased from 6s -> 12s in canary pool. (Ops roll 1743)
- Disable KV-cache compression fallback for sequences >1024 tokens in canary pools.
- Add alert refinement: new alert split-rate:sustained >15/min for any kernel host for >5m.

Longer-term actions (agreed in meeting)
- Action 1: Marcus to add a conservative memory-safety margin to the batch-size estimator + add unit tests covering compressed KV segments. Due: 2029-07-27.
- Action 2: Dana to instrument and trace KV deserialize refcounts and ownership handoffs to detect double-deserialize races. Due: 2029-07-25.
- Action 3: Evan to prototype an async-deserialize path that yields to kernel scheduler instead of blocking the CPU. PoC due: 2029-08-02.
- Action 4: Priya to run a 48h canary (west-2) with mitigations and gather microsecond traces and heap profiles. Begin: 2029-07-21.
- Action 5: Lina to update runbook and on-call playbook with the new split-rate alert and checklist for rolling the disabled-compression flag across regions. Due: 2029-07-22.

Design notes / implementation pointers for Marcus (batch estimator)
- Current estimator: uses avg_token_bytes * sequence_length + kv_page_overhead(lookup_count). Need to: (a) add measured decompress_peak_cpu_cost factor, (b) include compressed_on_disk_size * decompress_multiplier to estimate peak working set.
- Tests: synthesize sequences with artificially large sparse attention pages to validate margin. Hint: use loadgen payloads from testdata/kv-large-sparse/*.json.

Dana (KV deserialization tracing) guidance
- Add per-entry lifetime id and origin-tag (prefetch vs request-owned). Emit trace on first-deserialize and on free. Hook into flamegraph collector for 1s-sampled CPU stacks. Look for duplicate first-deserialize for same entry id within 200ms window.

Evan (async-deserialize) notes
- PoC: offload heavy deserialization into cooperative worker threads with a per-request future. Must ensure cancellation token semantics when split cancels request. Avoid synchronous memcpy in hot path. Baseline goal: reduce worst-case CPU blocking from 30–120ms to <8ms per now.

Follow-ups and meeting schedule
- Quick sync: 2029-07-22 09:00 PDT (30m) — owners only, check progress and decide canary rollout scale.
- Full weekly serving-runtime sync: 2029-07-25 11:00 PDT — present findings and next steps to eng leads.

Notes-to-self / fringe observations
- Split events spike more on hosts with older CUDA driver (11.7 vs 12.1); correlation needs controlled test.
- A few client traces show repeated requeue attempts caused by retry-policy interaction with split; consider adding jitter to client retry timings when split occurs.

Unresolved questions
- Is the compression fallback itself necessary for memory pressure cases, or would simply evicting older KV entries be cheaper?
- Can the batch-split heuristic be moved earlier in the request lifecycle without harming other latency SLOs?

Appendix: quick command snippets used during triage
- grep of split events: rg "batch_split" /var/log/serving-runtime/*.log | cut -d\" -f1-6 | head -n 200
- collect flamegraphs on host: sudo perf record -F 99 -p <pid> -g -- sleep 10; sudo perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl | flamegraph.pl > flame.svg
- heapprof: ./heap-profiler --pid <pid> --out /tmp/heap.json --duration 20s

If you pick up on this handoff: focus first on validating the mem_estimate path (Action 1 + Action 2). If both fail to explain, we prioritize Evan's async-deserialize PoC.

-- End of handoff --

Notes history: 2029-07-18 initial incident scribble, 2029-07-19 expanded telemetry and experiments, 2029-07-20 mitigations applied, 2029-07-21 handoff and action assignment.
